nodes.name: In situ CoFe-LDH growth on IF
nodes.procedure: CoFeLDH was grown in situ on the surface of iron foam (IF) through solution impregnation at room temperature, creating abundant oxygen vacancies on the CoFe-LDH as reported in our previous work [13]. Ultra-depth-of-field imaging (Figure S1) revealed the dense and uniform growth of CoFe-LDH from the interior to the surface of IF.

nodes.name: Dual Ru/Ir single atom impregnation
nodes.procedure: Ru and Ir single atoms were selectively anchored onto the oxygen vacancies of CoFe-LDH/IF via a one-step impregnation process. The elemental composition was determined using ICP-OES analysis, which revealed Ru and Ir contents of 0.065 and 1.405 wt.%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES analysis revealed Ru content of 0.065 wt% and Ir content of 1.405 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental composition of the synthesized material was precisely determined using Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-OES) analysis, which revealed Ru and Ir contents of 0.065 and 1.405 wt.%, respectively (Figure S2 and Table S1)

nodes.characterization_summary: CoFe-LDH possessed a well-defined nanoneedle morphology uniformly distributed across the iron foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) images (Figure 1b; Figures S3 and S4) revealed that the CoFe-LDH possessed a well-defined nanoneedle morphology that was uniformly distributed across the iron foam.
Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) images (Figure 1b; Figures S3 and S4) revealed that the CoFe-LDH possessed a well-defined nanoneedle morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice spacing of 0.196 nm attributable to the (018) crystal plane of CoFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further structural verification by high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) revealed a lattice spacing of 0.196 nm, attributable to the (018) crystal plane of CoFe-LDH (Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks corresponding to the (104), (015), (018), and (112) planes of CoFe-LDH with metallic iron and magnetite phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray Diffraction (XRD) analysis provided additional evidence of the successful formation of CoFe-LDH, with diffraction peaks corresponding to the (104), (015), (018), and (112) planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic-scale dispersion of Ru and Ir single atoms on CoFe-LDH/IF nanoneedles with uniformly distributed bright spots and intensity differences indicating heteronuclear metal atomic structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected High-Angle Annular Dark-Field Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (HAADF-STEM) imaging (Figure 1e,f) revealed the atomic-scale dispersion of Ru and Ir single atoms on the CoFe-LDH/IF nanoneedles.

properties.visualization: 2D density map with color gradient (blue to red)

nodes.characterization_summary: Negative shift in Fe 2p binding energy (0.77 eV) and Co 2p binding energy (0.57 eV); O1s peaks for adsorbed H2O, oxygen vacancies, M-OOH, and M-O; reduction in oxygen vacancy concentration after Ru/Ir incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was employed to examine the surface chemical states of Ru, Ir@CoFe-LDH/IF. A significant negative shift in the Fe 2p binding energy (0.77 eV) and the Co 2p binding energy (0.57 eV) was observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Signal at g = 2.003 characteristic of oxygen vacancies, with increased intensity in Ru, Ir@CoFe-LDH/IF compared to CoFe-LDH/IF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron Spin Resonance (ESR) spectroscopy provided complementary evidence of oxygen vacancies. Both Ru, Ir@CoFe-LDH/IF and CoFe-LDH/IF exhibited a signal at g = 2.003, characteristic of oxygen vacancies (Figure S9)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L3-edge XANES spectra show edge energy between IrCl3 and IrO2, indicative of cationic environment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ir L3-edge XANES spectra (Figure 2b) revealed that the edge energy of Ru, Ir@CoFe-LDH, lies between those of IrCl3 and IrO2, indicative of a cationic environment.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ir-O peak at 1.69 Å and diminished Ir-Ir peak; Ir-M coordination at 2.52 Å; Ir oxidation state 3.8+ with minimal Ir-Ir and Ru-Ir bonding.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier-transformed EXAFS (FT-EXAFS) spectrum (Figure 2c) showed an Ir-O peak at 1.69Å and a diminished Ir-Ir peak at higher shells, confirming the atomic dispersion of Ir atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir-O bond dominant with peaks at (1.69 Å, 5.26 Å⁻¹) and (2.63 Å, 8.71 Å⁻¹), consistent with IrO2 coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Wavelet Transform EXAFS (WT-EXAFS) analyses (Figure 2e; Figure S11) identified the Ir-O bond as the dominant coordination feature, with peaks at (1.69 Å, 5.26 Å⁻¹) and (2.63 Å, 8.71 Å⁻¹)

nodes.characterization_summary: Broad bands at 500-720 cm⁻¹ close to Eg/A1g modes of RuO2 and IrO2, indicating Ru-O and Ir-O coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Within the range of 300 - 800 cm⁻¹, the Raman spectrum of Ru, Ir@CoFe-LDH exhibits broad bands centered around 500-720 cm⁻¹, which are close to the Eg/Alg vibrational modes of RuO2 and IrO2

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl of 53.5 mF cm⁻² for Ru, Ir@CoFe-LDH/IF (2.45× CoFe-LDH/IF, 1.39× Ru@CoFe-LDH/IF, 1.08× Ir@CoFe-LDH/IF); Co²⁺/Co³⁺ oxidation peaks at 1.2-1.4 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru, Ir@CoFe-LDH/IF exhibits a Cdl of 53.5 mF cm⁻², which is 2.45 times that of CoFe-LDH/IF (21.8 mF cm⁻²), 1.39 times that of Ru@CoFe-LDH/IF (38.4 mF cm⁻²), and 1.08 times that of Ir@CoFe-LDH/IF (49.7 mF cm⁻²).
